Accepted [PrecisionStorage](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/ac0d9fb944cb5a81369d03c0c3bc5eab50ab6742/native/include/cybersand/precision_storage.hpp) is **eight bytes with eight-byte alignment**, including a 16-bit material field; the [Material enum](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/ac0d9fb944cb5a81369d03c0c3bc5eab50ab6742/native/include/cybersand/material.hpp) remains eight-bit. Likewise, a blanket “IN cannot have upward/negative vertical velocity” restriction is obsolete. Accepted [#406](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/pull/406) adds an identified signed IN-B1 option, and current Workbench exposes it. Unsigned-v1 behavior remains valid in its own scope; the optional law does not magically satisfy every liquid or submerged-volume requirement. State #20 and SIM-F18 are explicitly cross-linked. Current implementation establishes availability, not permanent policy.

Section: Milestone 1 state, persistence and generation research packet > 7. Save and Flatten
**Members:** #548, #572, related current owner clarification. Findings STATE-005, 020. [#548's dated 11 November correction](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/548) explicitly withdraws earlier World replacement, actor respawn, tick-zero reset, full physical continuation and complex rollback requirements. Its older [contract comment](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/548#issuecomment-6725828937) still names those behaviours; it is superseded evidence. The current owner wants the actual material layout after settling, erosion or reactions—not replayed original airborne oil/acid/water brushes. Explicit Flatten creates a **two-byte-per-cell** material baseline, retires old construction/history requirements and keeps the same live World. No general cell-carrier widening follows from LE16 storage. The active [#572](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/pull/572) source at snapshot **`8055a4a46f58b7afcd245ee344db2beb34ffb69c`** implements [bounded native bulk copy](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/8055a4a46f58b7afcd245ee344db2beb34ffb69c/native/include/cybersand/material_baseline.hpp) from `World::stored_material` into detached LE16 bytes under the existing exclusive owner. Its checks are not a lock; the caller must already own the World. The [authoring adoption](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/8055a4a46f58b7afcd245ee344db2beb34ffb69c/godot/scripts/shared_workbench.gd) changes the baseline, recipe/history references and related pending author responses without reconstructing physical World state. [The versioned container](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/8055a4a46f58b7afcd245ee344db2beb34ffb69c/godot/scripts/workbench_material_baseline.gd) stores bounded metadata plus the exact plane. [Native replacement](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/8055a4a46f58b7afcd245ee344db2beb34ffb69c/godot/native_extension/material_baseline_file.cpp) uses same-directory POSIX rename / Windows replace, with no predelete or copy/delete fallback; it explicitly does not promise general power-loss durability. This work is protected active integration. The refreshed issue body describes source qualification at `0b026f6b…`, while snapshot tip is `8055a4…` and runtime/provenance paths are in the diff. Do not infer final-tip technical GO from older body counts or pending package language; the root performs final delta refresh. Preserve genuine earlier prepared-host baseline omission and failed-owner recovery errors, plus harness negatives: an ineffective Windows source-lock probe and console-launcher RSS measurements. Correcting a fixture or measuring the real engine is not evidence that an original product failure never happened. Latest conversational owner intent also says ordinary Save should preserve the desired layout without unexpectedly destroying in-session Undo, maps need not always flatten, and no sweeping backward-compatibility guarantee is desired. Record that separately from historical evidence and the explicit active Flatten contract. This packet neither silently rewrites #572 nor turns it into a broad new save framework. Numeric ID reuse/remapping and actors/multiple layers are limits beyond a two-byte material plane; they are technical scope to resolve when that capability is implemented, not reasons to re-open settled intent. | Dimension | Assessment | |---|---| | Applicability | Concrete current authoring/history pain; active implementation addresses the explicit revised Flatten operation. | | Recoverable value | Owner clarification, LE16 copy/validation, authoring-only adoption, old-reader compatibility, atomic saved-start replacement and fault tests. | | Staleness | Old 8-bit estimates, reset/respawn/rollback contract, earlier source qualification status and invalid launcher memory observations. | | Philosophy / architecture | Practical material layout preservation; running physical state remains untouched,

The [executor](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/@MAIN@/godot/scripts/workbench_paint_editor_executor.gd#L131-L234) uses epoch, generation, tick/revision and settings/pause fences, actual native readback and explicit partial/complete outcomes. It does not reset actors/ticks or autosave. A later fresh load performs ordinary initialization; it is not a physical continuation snapshot. Those arithmetic sizes follow the specified encoding; they do not follow the current enum width or eight-byte runtime carrier. Nor does material-only Flatten satisfy GEN-006 dynamic persistence. **Separate fates.** Transfer accepted generator/PAINT coverage before considering old-ticket retirement. Section: Record schema and maintenance > Individual coverage records
Each item is keyed by its GitHub number and includes source URL/type, intake state, body SHA-256, timestamps, PR head/base identities where available, primary family, related items, findings, depth, confidence, limitations and explicit protection. The source index and portable evidence bundle retain the full intake response. `base-branch-at-intake` means a source branch relationship; it is never automatically translated into semantic adoption or a mandatory dependency. Four separate text fields record proposed fates: - `ticket_fate`: whether the historical obligation may later be consolidated, retained, superseded or retired. - `idea_fate`: current relevance and potential, independent of the ticket. - `code_fate`: adopted successor, selective donor, partial/unqualified implementation, rebuild candidate or no code. - `evidence_fate`: preserved positive/negative observations, tests, methods and missing originals. All records have `retirement_state: not-authorised`. The `protected` flag highlights active or paused integration/custody. A false flag grants no permission to touch a record or branch. The M1 authorisation permits only the capture branch and Draft/HOLD PR. `assessment_state` describes the investigation, not GitHub state. `transfer.state: captured-for-review` means that findings and dispositions have reached inspectable records. It is **not** a certification that every original artifact was recovered, every line was independently checked or retirement is safe. Original custody is separately itemised. Closed records use `indexed-only`; selected cited claims can be studied without falsely promoting the whole item to a completed assessment.
